statement: Whenever equal_pairs(grid) returns a result r, r equals the number of ordered pairs (i, j) with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n such that row i of grid equals column j of grid; equivalently, such that for every k with 0 <= k < n, grid[i][k] = grid[k][j].
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). Assume 1 <= n <= 200. Assume for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n. Assume for every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 100000.

statement: equal_pairs(grid) returns a result r (it does not fail) for every input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). Assume 1 <= n <= 200. Assume for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n. Assume for every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever equal_pairs(grid) returns a result r, 0 <= r <= n * n.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). Assume 1 <= n <= 200. Assume for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n. Assume for every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever equal_pairs(grid) returns a result r, r > 0 if and only if there exist indices i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n such that row i of grid equals column j of grid (i.e. for every k with 0 <= k < n, grid[i][k] = grid[k][j]).
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). Assume 1 <= n <= 200. Assume for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n. Assume for every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever equal_pairs(grid) returns a result r, r = n * n if and only if all entries of grid are equal, i.e. for every i, j, i', j' with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= j < n, 0 <= i' < n, and 0 <= j' < n, grid[i][j] = grid[i'][j'].
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). Assume 1 <= n <= 200. Assume for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n. Assume for every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever equal_pairs(grid) returns a result r, r >= d, where d is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n such that row i of grid equals column i of grid (i.e. for every k with 0 <= k < n, grid[i][k] = grid[k][i]).
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). Assume 1 <= n <= 200. Assume for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n. Assume for every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever equal_pairs(grid) returns a result r, r equals the number of ordered pairs (i, j) with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n such that row i of grid equals row j of grid (i.e. for every k with 0 <= k < n, grid[i][k] = grid[j][k]).
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). Assume 1 <= n <= 200. Assume for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n. Assume for every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 100000. Assume grid is symmetric: for every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] = grid[j][i].

statement: Whenever equal_pairs(grid) returns a result r, r also equals the number of ordered pairs (i, j) with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n such that column i of grid equals row j of grid (i.e. for every k with 0 <= k < n, grid[k][i] = grid[j][k]).
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). Assume 1 <= n <= 200. Assume for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n. Assume for every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever equal_pairs(grid) returns a result r, r equals the sum, over all length-n sequences v of 64-bit integers, of R(v) * C(v), where R(v) is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n such that row i of grid equals v, and C(v) is the number of indices j with 0 <= j < n such that column j of grid equals v. Only finitely many v have R(v) or C(v) nonzero.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). Assume 1 <= n <= 200. Assume for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n. Assume for every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever equal_pairs(grid) returns a result r, r equals the number of length-n sequences v of 64-bit integers that occur both as a row of grid and as a column of grid; that is, the number of v for which there exists i with 0 <= i < n and row i = v and there exists j with 0 <= j < n and column j = v.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). Assume 1 <= n <= 200. Assume for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n. Assume for every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 100000. Assume all rows are pairwise distinct: for every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, if row i equals row j then i = j. Assume all columns are pairwise distinct: for every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, if column i equals column j then i = j.

statement: Whenever equal_pairs(grid) returns a result r, r = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). Assume 1 <= n <= 200. Assume for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n. Assume for every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 100000. Assume all rows of grid are equal to the first row: for every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] = grid[0][j]. Assume the first row is not constant: there exist j, k with 0 <= j < n and 0 <= k < n such that grid[0][j] != grid[0][k].

statement: Whenever equal_pairs(grid) returns a result r, r = n.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). Assume 1 <= n <= 200. Assume for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(grid[i]) = n. Assume for every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 100000. Assume there exist values a and b with a != b such that for every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] = a if i = j, and grid[i][j] = b if i != j.
